_meta.description: Official sources polled by monitor.py for regulatory change detection (brief §21, §24, §39). Detecting a change here NEVER edits research/rule_seed_data.json or research/state_profiles.json directly — it only writes a RegulatoryChangeRecord to monitoring/change_log/ for human review. See the Detect->Review->Validate->Approve->Version->Test->Deploy workflow in REGULATORY_RESEARCH_REPORT.md.

sources.known_limitation: KNOWN LIMITATION, confirmed by this monitor's own output: irs.en.gov.ng is a JavaScript-rendered SPA. A plain HTTP fetch (used here) only retrieves the loading shell ('You need to enable JavaScript to run this app.'), not the real content that a browser renders. This source's hash will stay constant regardless of real content changes until the monitor is upgraded to a headless-browser fetch. Treat this entry as a placeholder for that upgrade, not as working coverage today.
Same SPA-shell limitation as esirs-tax-system — see that entry.

state_website_watchlist_note: Every row in research/state_profiles.json carries an official_website — monitor.py's --watch-all-states flag polls those too, purely as a superficial 'has this page changed' tripwire (new content hash) for the 34 states not yet FULLY_RESEARCHED. A changed hash there means 'go research this state properly', not 'a specific rule changed' — those states have no specific rules to diff against yet.
